en.title: Japan's PC & PlayStation Sales Surge 13% Fueled by Resident Evil Requiem
en.summary: Japan's PC and PlayStation gaming market experienced a significant 13% uplift in unit sales during the first half of 2026. This growth was largely propelled by the enduring popularity of the **Resident Evil** franchise, specifically **Resident Evil Requiem**.
en.body:
Japan's dedicated gaming audience continues to show robust enthusiasm for PC and console experiences, with the first half of 2026 marking a notable 13% increase in unit sales, reaching a total of 21 million. This surge, detailed in Sensor Tower's latest Japan Game Market Insights, indicates a healthy and growing market for traditional gaming platforms.

The primary driver behind this impressive growth appears to be the continued momentum of established franchises, with **Resident Evil Requiem** leading the charge. The survival horror giant has a long history of captivating Japanese players, and its latest installment clearly resonated, carrying franchise appeal into the sales figures. Beyond established titans, the market also benefited from fresh appeal brought by new titles. **PRAGMATA**, a highly anticipated AAA offering, alongside the intriguing indie concept **MECCCHA CHAMELEON**, injected new excitement and variety, attracting both seasoned players and newcomers.

This upswing isn't solely reliant on blockbuster releases. Sensor Tower's data also points to increased downloads and new releases contributing to the market's expansion. The report notes that both Steam and PlayStation platforms contributed comparable volumes, suggesting a balanced ecosystem where digital storefronts and console hardware are both thriving. This diversification of content, from major AAA productions to innovative indie projects, is crucial for sustaining engagement in a mature market.

## What This Means for Players

For fans in Japan, this means a vibrant and diverse gaming landscape. The success of **Resident Evil Requiem** underscores the power of beloved IPs to not only retain but also grow an audience. The inclusion of titles like **PRAGMATA** and **MECCCHA CHAMELEON** signals that developers are investing in new ideas for these platforms, offering exciting prospects for variety and innovation. This growth suggests that publishers are seeing strong returns on their investments in the Japanese PC and console space, which could translate into even more high-quality releases and ongoing support for live-service games.

## What's Next

While specific future titles driving the second half of 2026 are not yet detailed, the trend suggests continued investment from major publishers. Players can anticipate more AAA releases and a steady stream of indie gems on both Steam and PlayStation, building on the momentum established in the first half of the year. The report also hints at broader trends, with PC gaming celebrating "another record year" globally and mobile revenue remaining consistent, showcasing the multifaceted nature of the Japanese gaming economy.
